messages:
Lena (Design): throwing a different idea into the ring: instead of a tall latency card, what if we use a horizontal "chip" that contains the main stat (p95), a micro histogram inline, and a tiny chevron to expand for details. target: fit three chips per row on medium dashboards. feedback?
Priya (PM): sounds promising. Users want fast anomaly detection + quick jump to traces. chips should make it easy to scan many routes. default chip should emphasize p95 and a color state for regression.
Devon (Eng): inline histogram is feasible if we get pre-bucketed counts. we can return a compact array of 8-12 bins. perf note: computing exact buckets for every route and time window could be heavy at high cardinality. recommend pre-aggregating 1m histograms and merging on query.
Ravi (Data): agree. alternative is to ship a t-digest p95 + an 8-bin approximate histogram from sketches. API idea: `GET /metrics/latency?route=/checkout&window=15m&bins=8&approx=true` returns `p95: 230, bins: [120,80,30,...], sample_rate:0.1`. UI can show `sample_rate` and surface `~` or `approx` when sample_rate < 1.
Maya (Accessibility): a few accessibility constraints for chips: 
- color + shape alone can't convey regression state. add an icon (arrow up/down/—) and an ARIA live region for value updates.
- inline histograms must be keyboard reachable; focus should open the expanded view and expose the full histogram as a list so screen readers can parse bin ranges and counts.
- ensure the chip contrast and touch target meet 44px min for mobile.
Lena (Design): good calls. microcopy thoughts: primary label: `p95 230ms`, secondary line: `~10% sampled` when applicable. badge options: `~` icon with tooltip `Approximate (sampling)` and aria-label. on focus, show expanded panel with full histogram + link `Open traces`.
Priya (PM): copy for sampling confirm when turning off: short + clear. Proposal: `Disable sampling to compute exact metrics. This may increase query time and cost.` Button: `Run exact query (may take up to 30s)`.
Devon (Eng): implement as async job + poll. we should show progress and allow cancel. also record telemetry when users request exact runs to help sizing.
Ravi (Data): when we send `approx=true` we should also include `confidence` or `stderr` for the estimate so UI can render a subtle uncertainty indicator (faint blur or thinner bar).
Maya (Accessibility): uncertainty indicators must not rely on opacity alone. pair with textual hint `±20ms` or `low confidence` readout. screen readers should read the confidence after the metric.
Lena (Design): UX trade: minimal chip vs richer expanded view. plan: default chip (compact), hover/focus expands inline card with detailed histogram, percentiles list, sampling toggle and `Open traces` CTA. we'll prototype interaction states: hover, focus, keyboard-expand, and mobile tap.
Priya (PM): can we include small heatmap overlay for time-trend in expanded view? ops teams asked for quick trend sparkline colored by latency bucket.
Devon (Eng): heatmap overlay ok but heavier. for expanded view we can request a `trend_heatmap=true` endpoint that returns a 2D array for the time windows vs bins. we should cap resolution (e.g., 24x8) to keep payloads small.
Ravi (Data): also suggest caching the last successful exact-run result for 5 minutes to avoid repeat heavy queries. show `cached` tag if used.
Maya (Accessibility): last nit: interactive elements need clear focus rings and the expand chevron should have an aria-expanded state. also provide keyboard shortcuts (e.g., `t` to open traces from focused chip) — document these.
staging-bot: deployed chip-latency-preview to staging at https://staging.redwood/team/dashboards
Priya (PM): awesome. Lena, can you drop Figma links + interaction notes before EOD so eng can pair on API shape? We'll run a small playtest with a customer next week.
Lena (Design): will do. I'll mock compact chip + expanded panel and include alt text templates for the histogram. posting link in ~2 hours.
